observations: I opened assets/panels/05-2.png, main-cast.png and page-05.png with Read, and read responses/artwork-r2-05-2.json.
Ravi's identity matches the sheet: beard, thick brows, side part, green shirt and bag strap. His expression is curious and hopeful, with an open-mouth smile.
The phone is held at chest height with the screen toward the reader. The screen shows a calendar icon card, a heart icon card and blank colour blocks. There is no readable text or data.

Grip at panel scale: on the viewer-left edge, four fingertips with nails showing curl around the left edge onto the front. That is consistent with his right hand wrapping from behind, which is what the updated record says ('fingers wrapped around the left edge'). The viewer-right hand wears the wristwatch, so it is his left. It supports the lower right corner with the thumb on the screen edge, matching the record. I did not view the image at 200%.
The scene now records the camera as eye level, which matches the art. The monitor and plant are in the left foreground.

Earlier issue 1 (r2 eyeline): the image is unchanged and Ravi still glances up to screen-right. It is now recorded as a deliberate thinking glance, with Meera off-panel left. I find this acceptable for readers. His raised eyes and half-smile read as musing aloud rather than addressing someone on the right. The bubble's tail goes to his mouth, so the speaker is clear. On the page the glance also leads toward 05-3, where Meera answers, so the exchange still reads as one conversation. The screen direction is slightly off from 05-3, where he faces left, but it does not cause misreading.

Earlier issue 2 (r2 grip and record): resolved. The record now names the hand on each edge in Ravi's own left and right, and what I can see is consistent with the fingers wrapping from behind rather than a hand sitting flat in front of the phone.
Non-blocking record note: the prop's heldBy is 'ravi.right' while 'during' says both hands. If the field allows only one value this is tolerable, but it slightly understates the two-handed hold.

Lettering on page-05.png: the bubble at top-left has its tail to Ravi's mouth and clears his face. The WELBUK HEALTH label sits at bottom-left over the desk and ends just short of his right fingers. The phone screen stays clear.
